q: The discovery that a changing magnetic field could produce a current was made in 1831 by Michael Faraday and _____ working independently.
e: The discovery that a changing magnetic field could produce a current was made in 1831 by Michael Faraday and Joseph Henry working independently. Put Heinrich Lenz or Wilhelm Weber in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Faraday's law: induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop.

q: In a direct current, the electrons flow steadily in the same direction _____.
e: In a direct current, the electrons flow steadily in the same direction all the time. Put at regular time intervals or periodically in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. DC keeps one direction, the steady flow you get from a battery. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow.

q: The current that flows in power lines and normal household electricity from a wall outlet is _____ current.
e: The current that flows in power lines and normal household electricity from a wall outlet is alternating current. direct is not alternating, and induced is not alternating either. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: In Japan and in most of America, the voltage is between 100 V and _____ V.
e: In Japan and in most of America, the voltage is between 100 V and 120 V. 220 is not 120, and 240 is not 120 either. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: Europe and most other countries in the world, including Myanmar, use a voltage between 220V and _____ V.
e: Europe and most other countries in the world, including Myanmar, use a voltage between 220V and 240 V. Put 230 or 250 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: The frequency of AC current in Europe and most other parts of the world is _____ Hz.
e: The frequency of AC current in Europe and most other parts of the world is 50 Hz. 60 is not 50, and 100 is not 50 either. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: The waveform of the induced emf shown as a sine wave is represented by the equation $E = $ _____.
e: The waveform of the induced emf shown as a sine wave is represented by the equation E = Em sin ω t. Em cos ω t is not Em sin ω t, and Em sin t is not Em sin ω t either. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current.

q: The angular velocity $\omega$ is equal to _____, where $f$ is the frequency of the emf.
e: The angular velocity ω is equal to 2pi f, where f is the frequency of the emf. Put pi f or 2pi / f in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: The magnitude of an alternating current at any instant varies precisely the same way as the emf and is given by $I = $ _____.
e: The magnitude of an alternating current at any instant varies precisely the same way as the emf and is given by I = Im sin ω t. Put Im cos ω t or Im ω t in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: The inevitable loss of energy that occurs when current is distributed over long distances is far smaller with alternating current at high voltage and _____ current.
e: The inevitable loss of energy that occurs when current is distributed over long distances is far smaller with alternating current at high voltage and low current. Put high or zero in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: A rotating coil in a magnetic field is the basic principle of an AC generator, which is a device for generating _____ current.
e: A rotating coil in a magnetic field is the basic principle of an AC generator, which is a device for generating alternating current. Put direct or steady in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

q: A current flows through a loop of wire whenever there is a change in the magnetic lines of force through the loop; this phenomenon is called _____ induction.
e: A current flows through a loop of wire whenever there is a change in the magnetic lines of force through the loop; this phenomenon is called electromagnetic induction. electrostatic is not electromagnetic, and mutual is not electromagnetic either. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: The magnetic flux density $B$ is related to magnetic field strength $H$ by the equation $B = $ _____.
e: The magnetic flux density B is related to magnetic field strength H by the equation B = µ H. Put µ / H or H / µ in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Flux density B is magnetic lines through unit area perpendicular to the field. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

q: The permeability of free space (vacuum) $\mu_0$ is equal to _____ $H m^{-1}$.
e: The permeability of free space (vacuum) µ0 is equal to 4pi × 10^-7 H m^-1. Put 4pi × 10^-6 or 2pi × 10^-7 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The power 10^-7 is the conversion for this unit; a nearby prefix is a different size.

q: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is the tesla (T), which is equivalent to _____ per metre squared.
e: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is the tesla (T), which is equivalent to ampere per metre squared. weber is not ampere, and volt is not ampere either. Flux density B is magnetic lines through unit area perpendicular to the field.

q: In electromagnetism, the magnetic flux through a surface is the surface integral of the _____ component of the magnetic field $B$ over that surface.
e: In electromagnetism, the magnetic flux through a surface is the surface integral of the normal component of the magnetic field B over that surface. tangential and parallel belong to other processes, not this normal case. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

q: If the magnetic field is uniform over a plane area $A$, the magnetic flux $\Phi$ passing through that area is simply $\Phi = $ _____.
e: If the magnetic field is uniform over a plane area A, the magnetic flux Phi passing through that area is simply Phi = BA cos θ. BA sin θ is not BA cos θ, and B/A cos θ is not BA cos θ either. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

q: When the magnetic field is parallel to the surface area, the angle $\theta$ is $90^\circ$ and the magnetic flux $\Phi$ is equal to _____.
e: When the magnetic field is parallel to the surface area, the angle θ is 90^° and the magnetic flux Phi is equal to zero. Put maximum or BA in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.

q: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the _____, named after the German physicist Wilhelm Eduard Weber.
e: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber, named after the German physicist Wilhelm Eduard Weber. Put tesla or henry in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

q: Magnetic field strength and magnetic flux density are vector quantities, whereas magnetic flux is a _____ quantity.
e: Magnetic field strength and magnetic flux density are vector quantities, whereas magnetic flux is a scalar quantity. tensor is not scalar, and pseudo-vector is not scalar either. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Flux density B is magnetic lines through unit area perpendicular to the field.

q: Faraday's law states that the magnitude of induced emf in a wire loop is directly proportional to the rate of change of _____ through that loop.
e: Faraday's law states that the magnitude of induced emf in a wire loop is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through that loop. electric field is not magnetic flux, and magnetic density is not magnetic flux either. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

q: For a wire loop with $N$ identical turns, the induced emf $E$ is given by the equation $E = $ _____.
e: For a wire loop with N identical turns, the induced emf E is given by the equation E = -N (dPhiB)/(dt). Put N (dPhiB)/(dt) or -N PhiB t in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current.

q: In Faraday's law equation, the minus sign gives the _____ of the induced emf.
e: In Faraday's law equation, the minus sign gives the direction of the induced emf. magnitude is not direction, and resistance is not direction either. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current.

q: An induced emf is always in a direction that opposes the change in the original magnetic flux that causes it; this statement is known as _____ Law.
e: An induced emf is always in a direction that opposes the change in the original magnetic flux that causes it; this statement is known as Lenz's Law. Put Faraday's or Fleming's in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Lenz's law sets the sign: the induced emf fights the flux change that made it.

q: Lenz's law is a good example of the principle of conservation of _____.
e: Lenz's law is a good example of the principle of conservation of energy. Put momentum or mass in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Lenz's law sets the sign: the induced emf fights the flux change that made it.

q: When a magnet is moved towards a coil, the magnetic flux through the coil increases, and the induced current must produce a magnetic field which _____ an increase in the original magnetic flux.
e: When a magnet is moved towards a coil, the magnetic flux through the coil increases, and the induced current must produce a magnetic field which opposes an increase in the original magnetic flux. Put supports or doubles in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

q: If the wire loop is not moving or is moving parallel to the magnetic field lines, there is _____ induced emf.
e: If the wire loop is not moving or is moving parallel to the magnetic field lines, there is no induced emf. Put maximum or minimum in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.

q: In 1851, a German instrument maker named Heinrich Ruhmkorff showed how an electric spark could be produced using an apparatus called an _____ coil.
e: In 1851, a German instrument maker named Heinrich Ruhmkorff showed how an electric spark could be produced using an apparatus called an induction coil. Put transformer or ignition in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The year 1851 belongs to this fact, not a nearby discovery date.

q: In an induction coil, the primary coil consists of a few turns of _____ insulated wire.
e: In an induction coil, the primary coil consists of a few turns of thick insulated wire. Put thin or bare in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Primary takes the AC supply; secondary delivers power to the load, with voltages in the turns ratio.

q: In an induction coil, a _____ is connected across the contacts to prevent sparking and wearing away of contacts.
e: In an induction coil, a capacitor is connected across the contacts to prevent sparking and wearing away of contacts. resistor is not capacitor, and inductor is not capacitor either. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The induction coil is commonly used in the _____ system of motor cars.
e: The induction coil is commonly used in the ignition system of motor cars. Put braking or cooling in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The induction coil is commonly used in the _____ system of motor cars. ignition.

q: Most generators give out alternating current and are also called _____.
e: Most generators give out alternating current and are also called alternators. transformers and rectifiers belong to other processes, not this alternators case. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: In a simple AC generator, the induced current flows through the two slip rings and then through the external load via two fixed _____ brushes.
e: In a simple AC generator, the induced current flows through the two slip rings and then through the external load via two fixed carbon brushes. Put copper or iron in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current.

q: Every time the coil in an AC generator turns through _____, the current reverses its direction.
e: Every time the coil in an AC generator turns through 180^°, the current reverses its direction. Put 90^° or 360^° in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

q: The induced electromotive force of a generator can be increased by increasing the area, the number of turns, using stronger magnets, and increasing the speed of _____.
e: The induced electromotive force of a generator can be increased by increasing the area, the number of turns, using stronger magnets, and increasing the speed of rotation. Put translation or vibration in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: For a coil of $N$ loops rotating with constant angular velocity $\omega$, the induced emf is $E = NBA\omega \sin \omega t$, where the maximum emf $E_m = $ _____.
e: For a coil of N loops rotating with constant angular velocity ω, the induced emf is E = NBAω sin ω t, where the maximum emf Em = NBAω. Put NBA or NBω in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current.

q: In an electric motor, electrical energy is used to rotate the coil to provide mechanical energy, whereas in a generator, _____ energy is used to rotate the coil to produce electrical energy.
e: In an electric motor, electrical energy is used to rotate the coil to provide mechanical energy, whereas in a generator, mechanical energy is used to rotate the coil to produce electrical energy. Put chemical or thermal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field.

q: A transformer is used to change the _____ of an alternating current.
e: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current. frequency is not voltage, and phase is not voltage either. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

q: The core of a transformer is built up of thin iron sheets of high resistance, called _____.
e: The core of a transformer is built up of thin iron sheets of high resistance, called lamination. mumetal is not lamination, and insulation is not lamination either. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

q: In a transformer, the coil connected to an alternating voltage source is called the _____ coil.
e: In a transformer, the coil connected to an alternating voltage source is called the primary coil. Put secondary or tertiary in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: The use of a laminated iron core in a transformer is to minimize the power loss due to the induced current flowing in the core, which are called _____ currents.
e: The use of a laminated iron core in a transformer is to minimize the power loss due to the induced current flowing in the core, which are called eddy currents. drift and displacement belong to other processes, not this eddy case. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: In an ideal transformer with no power losses, the power input is _____ to the power output.
e: In an ideal transformer with no power losses, the power input is equal to the power output. Put greater or less in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

q: The ratio of the induced emfs in the primary and secondary coils of a transformer is equal to the ratio of the number of _____ in the coils.
e: The ratio of the induced emfs in the primary and secondary coils of a transformer is equal to the ratio of the number of turns in the coils. Put volts or amperes in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. Primary takes the AC supply; secondary delivers power to the load, with voltages in the turns ratio.

q: If the secondary has more turns than the primary, the voltage obtained from the secondary is greater than the voltage applied to the primary; such a transformer is called a _____ transformer.
e: If the secondary has more turns than the primary, the voltage obtained from the secondary is greater than the voltage applied to the primary; such a transformer is called a step-up transformer. step-down and isolation belong to other processes, not this step-up case. Step-up means more secondary turns, higher secondary voltage, smaller secondary current. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

q: Transformers work on AC, but not on DC, because unless there is a _____ current in the input coil, no voltage is induced in the output coil.
e: Transformers work on AC, but not on DC, because unless there is a changing current in the input coil, no voltage is induced in the output coil. steady is not changing, and high is not changing either. DC keeps one direction, the steady flow you get from a battery.

q: To improve the efficiency of a transformer, _____ magnetic material should be used to make the core.
e: To improve the efficiency of a transformer, soft magnetic material should be used to make the core. Put hard or permanent in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

q: Most transformers have a full load efficiency ranging from 95% to _____ %.
e: Most transformers have a full load efficiency ranging from 95% to 98. 5 %. Put 99. 9 or 100 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics.

q: The efficiency of a transformer is defined as the ratio of the _____ power to the input power.
e: The efficiency of a transformer is defined as the ratio of the output power to the input power. Put apparent or reactive in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

q: The electricity generated at the power station is transmitted to the consumers through the _____ cables.
e: The electricity generated at the power station is transmitted to the consumers through the power cables. Put signal or control in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Power station is transmitted to the consumers through the _____ cables. power.

q: One of the main problems in the long distance transmission of electricity is power loss in the form of _____.
e: One of the main problems in the long distance transmission of electricity is power loss in the form of heat. Put light or sound in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Transmission of electricity is power loss in the form of _____. heat.

q: The amount of electrical power lost as heat in a transmission line is given by the formula $P_{loss} = $ _____.
e: The amount of electrical power lost as heat in a transmission line is given by the formula Ploss = I^2 R. Put I R^2 or V^2 / I in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R.

q: A practical way to reduce power loss in transmission cables is to reduce the magnitude of the transmission current by stepping up the _____.
e: A practical way to reduce power loss in transmission cables is to reduce the magnitude of the transmission current by stepping up the voltage. Put resistance or frequency in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: The _____ grid system is used to distribute electricity around the country, allowing power stations in low demand areas to supply high demand areas.
e: The national grid system is used to distribute electricity around the country, allowing power stations in low demand areas to supply high demand areas. local is not national, and private is not national either. Power stations in low demand areas to supply high demand areas. national.

q: In the national grid system, the voltage is first stepped up for transmission and finally stepped down at the _____ in stages before it is used in factories and homes.
e: In the national grid system, the voltage is first stepped up for transmission and finally stepped down at the substations in stages before it is used in factories and homes. generators is not substations, and meters is not substations either. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: Electricity supplied to the house is a single-phase form of alternating current, carried by a thick cable containing the live wire and the _____ wire.
e: Electricity supplied to the house is a single-phase form of alternating current, carried by a thick cable containing the live wire and the neutral wire. earth is not neutral, and ground is not neutral either. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: The live wire is a dangerous wire as it carries a high voltage, while the neutral wire is usually at _____ volt.
e: The live wire is a dangerous wire as it carries a high voltage, while the neutral wire is usually at zero volt. Put maximum or half in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The live conductor swings plus and minus and is the dangerous one. Neutral is held near zero by the supply company and completes the loop.

q: The electricity is fed into the house through the main fuse, meter, main switch, and then to the _____ box.
e: The electricity is fed into the house through the main fuse, meter, main switch, and then to the distribution box. junction is not distribution, and connection is not distribution either. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: In the new wiring colour code, the colour for the live wire (L) is _____.
e: In the new wiring colour code, the colour for the live wire (L) is brown. blue is not brown, and green-yellow is not brown either. The live conductor swings plus and minus and is the dangerous one.

q: In the new wiring colour code, the colour for the neutral wire (N) is _____.
e: In the new wiring colour code, the colour for the neutral wire (N) is brown. Put blue or red in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Neutral is held near zero by the supply company and completes the loop.

q: In the new wiring colour code, the striped green-yellow colour is used for the _____ wire.
e: In the new wiring colour code, the striped green-yellow colour is used for the earth wire. Put live or neutral in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Code, the striped green-yellow colour is used for the _____ wire. earth.

q: In the lighting circuit, the light bulbs are arranged in _____ across the mains line so that switching OFF one bulb does not affect the others.
e: In the lighting circuit, the light bulbs are arranged in parallel across the mains line so that switching OFF one bulb does not affect the others. Put series or sequence in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: A lighting circuit must be connected sequentially as live wire, fuse, switch, load, and then to the _____ wire.
e: A lighting circuit must be connected sequentially as live wire, fuse, switch, load, and then to the live wire. Put earth or neutral in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The live conductor swings plus and minus and is the dangerous one.

q: A power circuit is an electrical system in which distribution points are connected to the main supply in a continuous closed circuit, also known as a _____ main circuit.
e: A power circuit is an electrical system in which distribution points are connected to the main supply in a continuous closed circuit, also known as a delta main circuit. Put star or ring in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A ring main feeds sockets both ways around a loop so cable current is shared.

q: The power circuit supplies electricity to all the wall sockets and uses thinner wires because the current can flow to any particular socket by _____ ways.
e: The power circuit supplies electricity to all the wall sockets and uses thinner wires because the current can flow to any particular socket by two ways. Put three or four in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: Each main ring circuit typically uses a _____ A fuse.
e: Each main ring circuit typically uses a 30 A fuse. Put 15 or 50 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: The heating circuit is used for appliances like electric cookers and washing machines, and each fuse used in such a circuit is rated at _____ A.
e: The heating circuit is used for appliances like electric cookers and washing machines, and each fuse used in such a circuit is rated at 30 A. 5 is not 30, and 10 is not 30 either. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: The fuse of each circuit must be connected in the _____ lead and must never be in the neutral lead.
e: The fuse of each circuit must be connected in the live lead and must never be in the neutral lead. earth is not live, and ground is not live either. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: A circuit breaker is an automatic switch which trips when the current rises above the specified value, and it can be reset by turning the switch ON or pressing a _____.
e: A circuit breaker is an automatic switch which trips when the current rises above the specified value, and it can be reset by turning the switch ON or pressing a button. Put lever or dial in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A breaker is a reusable automatic switch that trips on overload or a short.

q: Earthing of an electrical appliance connects specific parts of an electric power system with the ground, typically the earth's conductive surface, for _____ purposes.
e: Earthing of an electrical appliance connects specific parts of an electric power system with the ground, typically the earth's conductive surface, for aesthetic purposes. safety is not aesthetic, and functional is not aesthetic either. Earth bonding dumps a fault current so the case cannot stay live.

q: In any electrical appliance, the earth wire is always connected to the _____ case.
e: In any electrical appliance, the earth wire is always connected to the metal case. Put plastic or wooden in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Earth bonding dumps a fault current so the case cannot stay live.

q: With proper earthing, if a loose live wire touches the metal case, the current passes directly into the earth through the earth wire because it has much _____ resistance than a human being.
e: With proper earthing, if a loose live wire touches the metal case, the current passes directly into the earth through the earth wire because it has much smaller resistance than a human being.
